script: AddText "The docking bay to The Factory teems with smaller ships bringing in cargo from the extra-orbital mining operations within the Fireworks Belt. The lucky operators just about cover their living costs after they have settled the issue of 'protection'. Empty, angry eyes abound - with heavy-armoured Syndicate Marines on every corner." marketFlavorTextColor

AddText "The incessant rumble of the systems sweeping volatiles from the surface of Nearly There make civilised conversation impractical, and the unusual practice of mixing personnel transit routes with conduits for the gaseous volatiles makes unaccompanied exploration inadvisable. The dock-hands give all crew (on arrival) foam ear-plugs, specialised breathing apparatus and an illustrated guide to the station with a central fold-out map." marketFlavorTextColor

AddText "The irregular dull drumming of debris shunts the heavily armoured carapace of this station, erected and operated in the honour of a long dead Naval commander of questionable achievement and repute - Karkov. Her image hangs from the central domical light by thick steel cabling. Welding drones hum as they hover amongst the high arched ceilings constantly repairing and refurbishing the buckling walls and struts, shifting almost visibly under the pressure of the external battering. The strobing flashes from welding torches light up the main hall highlighting the blue and red uniforms of hundreds of the next generation of the Junk Pirates Navy, almost all of them appear to be drunk. The air is thick with alcohol and the taste of hot metal." marketFlavorTextColor

AddText "The hab-tubes echo - almost glow - with the reverberant noise of laughter and conversation. It is difficult to hear anything with people shouting over the top of other people shouting in the main thoroughfares, whilst the stores, workshops and living spaces accessible immediately through heavy, bronze-tinged ceramic doors, are eerily quiet. The symbol of Glory hiding in the shadow of the red star Breh'Inni recurs throughout most spaces." marketFlavorTextColor

AddText "The artificial, dendritically branching network of high-pressure, radiation-proof habitations on this near-star world are oppressive and the atmosphere is thick. Nevertheless the pirates, brigands and artists that call this place home are unusually warm to visitors. Any visitor to this frontier world is given a free reign, and treated with great respect as a matter of course - those that live here are safe in the knowledge that any misstep will quickly see them ejected on to the exceptionally hot surface of the planet that is only ever a few tens of metres away from anywhere you could ever be." marketFlavorTextColor

AddText "The number of adverts hawking the services of the ASP Syndicate are almost unbearable, and each one seems to be designed to be more eye-catching than the last. Neon lights and rapidly repeating beat-based musical interludes punctuate your interactions with the locals - who seem - as a rule - content, healthy and relatively wealthy." marketFlavorTextColor
AddText "The smell of soap is all-encompassing, a (fortunate) by-product of whatever is going on in the ubiquitous chemical processing filtration plants throughout Yogi." marketFlavorTextColor

The symbol of Glory hiding in the shadow of the red star Breh'Inni recurs throughout most spaces." marketFlavorTextColor

AddText "The hab-tubes in the main thoroughfares are generally quiet and sparsely populated. Locals mutter of the completion of the Exodus - and a change in fortunes. The three-toed paw of the Post Anarchist Canis Kollective has been stamped in ink against most doors." marketFlavorTextColor

AddText "A large, traditional woven tapestry of the Three-Toed Paw of the P.A.C.K. greets you at the dock gate, alongside a group of locals. They welcome you in, but warn you (seriously) to steer clear of the forbidden areas. A loop plays on the holo-screen projector describing the opportunities for enterprising individuals on Christchurch." marketFlavorTextColor

AddText "Ship traffic is busy with the movement of freighters and light escorts - there are those bringing minerals on-board the station and those taking them further afield. Inventory system holo-projections blink in and out of existence as dockers process loads, with automated cranes and drone-shuttles sliding along rails and through the volume of the bay organising kiloton upon kiloton of the asteroidal hoard." marketFlavorTextColor

AddText "Visitors are less common at this sparsely populated station, and the folk around the place tend to smile in a sinister way. Hawkers hand out invites to phenomemonally expensive-to-view no-rules fight events, giving away luridly coloured drinks in bulbous smoking vials to sweeten the invite. Unexplained dark stains streak against most walls." marketFlavorTextColor
